HEARTHLANDS: Road is muddy past the mill.
The creek is high enough that I would use the bridge.
FRONTIER: Past the last farms, roads stop being somebody’s daily responsibility.
Pack for the trip once the maintained road gives out.
WILDLANDS: People come back with fewer landmarks they trust out there.
If you leave the old road, leave yourself a way back to it.
DREAD_REACHES: The older route notes get thin beyond the last known marker.
Out there, a familiar landmark is worth more than a short route.

HEARTHLANDS: Cold kept the tracks clean this morning.
Stay near the bank even when the river looks solid.
FRONTIER: Past the treeline, wind matters more than distance.
The pass is usable today; that is not the same as safe tomorrow.
WILDLANDS: We stopped maintaining that pass. Anyone farther out carries shelter.
A clear ridge can disappear in one change of weather.
DREAD_REACHES: The old ice chart has one route I still trust. One.
Past that shelf, even veteran travelers wait for visibility.

HEARTHLANDS: Rain put the low path under water again.
Keep the river on your left and the crossing is hard to miss.
FRONTIER: The trail disappears under roots after enough rain.
Use the high bank; the short path floods first.
WILDLANDS: We mark routes by crossings now. Paths do not last.
The canopy hides distance, so count river bends instead.
DREAD_REACHES: Past that bend, even the old survey notes stop agreeing.
The growth closes routes faster than people can reopen them.

HEARTHLANDS: Cross the open road early. Shade disappears by noon.
Water first, then distance. The road will still be there.
FRONTIER: The caravan road is longer, but it reaches water.
Do not trade a known well for a straight line.
WILDLANDS: Out there, a good well is a landmark and a plan.
A mesa can look close for half a day. Trust the route, not your eyes.
DREAD_REACHES: The old route assumes two wells. One is gone.
Beyond the last caravan marker, every shade stop matters.

HEARTHLANDS: Bears are into the lower orchard again.
Fog sits thick on the old road before sunrise.
FRONTIER: The old markers vanish in fog before the road does.
Past the timber turn, use the hedgerow until the track returns.
WILDLANDS: The strange reports keep starting beyond the same abandoned lane.
The woodline is familiar until the old road stops being used.
DREAD_REACHES: People still use the old names. They just do not use the roads.
Past the last orchard, the family maps become warnings more than routes.

STRANGER: I can tell you the public road. Anything else, ask around.
Nothing personal. I do not hand private village business to every traveler.
RECOGNIZED: You helped here before. I can give you more than the board notice.
I remember what you did. Ask me what you actually need.
RELIABLE: You have been right often enough that people will answer you plainly.
There is a part of this we did not put on the public notice.
TRUSTED: If I mark this for you, I expect you to tell us what changed.
We would rather ask you than send three people who do not know the ground.
PROVEN: You know what lies beyond the marker better than most of us now.
No one is ordering you. We are asking because you have earned the choice.

STRUCTURE_SURVEY: People keep describing the place differently. Somebody needs to settle what is actually there.
COMMUNITY_INCIDENT: It is small until it happens three mornings in a row. Then it becomes village business.
ECOLOGY: I want to know whether the animal is passing through or living beside us before anyone calls it a hunt.
ROAD: The road is still there. The question is whether people can use it safely.
WATER: The water changed after the last weather. That changes every route around it.
CAVE: The entrance is known. What changed below it is not.
RECENT_EVENT: Yesterday changed how people are using this part of the village.

STRUCTURE_SURVEY: Your survey settled the argument. Now we know what that place actually is.
COMMUNITY_INCIDENT: It has been quiet since you handled it. People noticed.
ECOLOGY: Since your report, nobody is treating every sighting like an attack.
ROAD: The first cart used that road again this morning.
WATER: The crossing is being used again. We are still watching the level.
CAVE: Your route notes are with the people who actually go underground.
RECENT_EVENT: Repairs are moving faster now that the immediate danger is over.

RAIN: Rain erased the older tracks, so anything sharp-edged out there is recent.
The low route is worse after this much rain.
SNOW: Fresh snow helps with tracks and hides old road markers.
Visibility is the bigger problem once the ridge disappears.
HEAT: Take the shaded route even if it costs distance.
Open ground is easier before the day gets hot.
FOG: Use the road edge, not the far treeline, until the fog lifts.
The old markers are easy to walk past in this.
RAID_RECENT: The wall held. Now the work is counting what did not.
Patrols are checking the roads for stragglers.
HORDE_RECENT: People heard the fighting from every house. The village is still taking stock.
There is repair work after a horde that a sword cannot do.
BLOOD_MOON_RECENT: That night left tracks everywhere. Sorting old sign from new will take time.
ROAD_DAMAGED: The shorter road is not the sensible road until repairs finish.

FIRST_MEETING: I do not think we have spoken before. What are you looking for?
KNOWN_FACE: Good to see you back. What changed?
You know the village now. Ask plainly.
HIGH_TRUST: I was hoping you would come by.
You already know the public version. Here is the part that matters.

UNKNOWN: I do not know. Ask someone whose work puts them closer to it.
Wrong person for that. I can tell you who I would trust instead.
RUMOR: I only heard it secondhand. Ask the person who actually saw it.
There is a story going around, but I would rather send you to the source.
LEAD: I can get you near it. For the exact place, talk to the person who keeps the route.
I know the approach; someone else knows the thing at the end of it.
KNOWN: I know the place. If you want the history rather than the route, ask the records keeper.
I can mark it. For what lives there now, ask someone with current field evidence.
CONFIRMED: You have been there yourself. If you need a second opinion, ask the specialist about what you brought back.

local_observation: I heard it from the upper field, not from somebody in the tavern.
profession_evidence: The evidence fits what I work with every day.
I am confident about the sign, not about the story attached to it.
village_report: Two people reported the same thing. I still did not see it myself.
That came from another resident, so I will tell you who.
map_record: It is on the older chart.
The route exists in the survey copy, though I cannot promise its current condition.
old_record: The name appears in an old record.
A century-old account can identify a place without describing today.
player_report: You were there. Your report outranks our rumor.
If you saw it yourself, I will stop calling it hearsay.
world_event: The change started after the storm.
We did not have this problem before the raid.
rumor_network: People keep saying it. Nobody has shown me proof.
That is village talk, not a fact I would put on a map.
quest_proof: What you brought back settles part of the question.
That proof is better than three more stories.

WHERE_EXACTLY: Answer at the precision permitted by knowledge state; never fabricate coordinates.
CAN_YOU_MARK_IT: Only KNOWN may mark the target directly; LEAD may mark a truly known intermediate landmark.
WHO_SAW_IT: Name the persistent witness when speaker knows them; otherwise state the provenance honestly.
HOW_DANGEROUS: Describe profession-specific evidence and uncertainty, not hidden difficulty numbers.
WHO_ELSE_WOULD_KNOW: Give persistent name plus profession/landmark context when possible.
WHAT_AM_I_LOOKING_FOR: Give a profession-specific visible cue the speaker could plausibly know.
